system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s “[STANDARD]” labels and efficiency note are not evidence of Buyer agreement. All positions remain reviewable. This review uses only the supplied documents, not the underlying DD records or full SPA. Numerical counterproposals below are suggested Buyer negotiating positions.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What Buyer should want | Recommendation — one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General warranties capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | A materially higher general cap, with separate treatment for fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities and fraud. | **Counter at 50% / AUD 12m**, subject to DD and recovery security; do not let the general cap absorb separately negotiated protections — 20% leaves substantial acquisition risk with Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, recovering only the excess. | Lower thresholds, a tipping basket and aggregation of related claims; specified categories excluded. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 100,000 tipping basket**, with related claims aggregated and fundamental, tax, specific indemnity and fraud claims outside these thresholds — the proposed deductible materially erodes recovery. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General claims notified within **18 months**; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least two annual reporting cycles, reasonable notice requirements and preservation of timely notified contingent claims. | **Seek 24–36 months for general warranties**, with separate category deadlines and no automatic forfeiture for immaterial notice defects — 18 months may expire before latent issues emerge. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title receive the same cap and time limit as general warranties. | Separate warranties covering authority, ownership, all issued shares, valid issue, fully paid status and freedom from encumbrances. | **Reject general-regime treatment; seek at least a 100%-of-price cap, no thresholds and a substantially longer period**, aligned with applicable limitation rules — Buyer must have meaningful recourse if it does not acquire what it paid for. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to **all Claims of any nature**; no express fraud exception supplied. | An express fraud carve-out from caps, thresholds, deadlines, disclosure/knowledge defences, non-reliance and exclusive-remedy restrictions. | **Require a comprehensive fraud carve-out**, covering Seller fraud and fraud attributable to Seller, while preserving non-excludable rights — contractual protections must not shelter fraudulent conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the indexed data room, referenced material, accounts, registers and public records. | Only sufficiently detailed, fair disclosure against relevant warranties; a fixed, accessible and retained disclosure bundle. | **Reject blanket/deemed disclosure; require specific, intelligible disclosure of nature and scope**, with any permitted general disclosures narrowly defined — document availability does not establish that a risk was fairly disclosed. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Bars claims for Buyer/adviser knowledge, including anything discoverable in the data room or public records. | No constructive, imputed or adviser-wide knowledge bar; preferably no independent knowledge exclusion. | **Delete; fallback limited to actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer deal principals**, without a duty of inquiry and excluding specific indemnities — “discoverable” risks transferring undiscovered liabilities to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied by delivery of written consent, despite outstanding associated conditions. | Effective consent satisfying clauses 11.2–11.3, with no unacceptable amendments, payments or continuing conditions. | **Make satisfactory consent and satisfaction of associated conditions a Buyer-waivable completion condition**, with evidence and a long-stop termination right — approximately 30% of revenue is exposed, and a consent letter alone may be insufficient. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release follows Completion. | Debt repayment and effective security release at or before Completion, with no residual guarantees or secured exposure. | **Require a verified payout letter, controlled simultaneous repayment and binding discharge/release arrangements**; deduct debt through agreed price mechanics without double counting — Buyer should not complete with Seller debt or enforceable security outstanding. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional completion bonuses are “for Seller” but absent from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Seller bears transaction-triggered bonuses and applicable superannuation, payroll tax and other on-costs, with payment responsibility documented. | **Expressly allocate these amounts to Seller and include them in the completion calculation/funds flow**, using a deduction, payment or retention without double counting — otherwise the acquired company may fund Seller’s transaction obligations. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; **AUD 180,000** recorded open, with no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. | Verified payment and effective ownership of all relevant project IP, plus protection against defective title and associated claims. | **Require payment verification and an effective assignment/confirmation before Completion, backed by a broader specific indemnity** — paying the invoice alone does not establish that all required IP rights have vested. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material; access, scope and notification requirements remain unresolved. | Prompt investigation, evidence preservation, containment and legally informed notification assessment, with pre-Completion incident risk allocated to Seller. | **Require an investigation/update covenant and a tailored specific indemnity, supported by retention if warranted** — uncertainty is not evidence of immateriality, but the present record does not establish a confirmed breach or loss. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals, **AUD 330,000 aggregate**, characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. | Verification of timing, relatedness, scope, cancellation rights, accrual and whether commitments required Buyer approval. | **Assess the renewals together under interim operating covenants and completion accounting; require consent for non-ordinary-course commitments** — neither ordinary-course status nor a price deduction follows automatically from the disclosed amounts. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | General limitations and remedies apply across all Claims unless expressly displaced. | Distinct regimes for general warranties, fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities, payment/completion obligations and fraud. | **Insert an express category matrix and precedence clause**, identifying applicable caps, thresholds, deadlines and exclusions — otherwise broad boilerplate can nullify bespoke protections. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | DD-012 share register records Seller as holder of 100% of issued shares. | Independent verification of issued capital, ownership, authority, encumbrances, options/convertibles and valid transfer mechanics. | **Reconcile the register with corporate records, issuance/transfer documents and relevant searches; require completion transfers, certificates or appropriate replacements, and releases** — the register is important evidence, not a complete title investigation. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties said to be settled under the general regime. | Separate tax protection and adequate IP warranties, distinct from the known Ironquay issue. | **Reopen expressly: seek a pre-Completion tax indemnity with a suitable longer period, commonly seven years subject to assessment rules, and separately negotiate IP scope, cap and survival** — the Seller’s assertion of settlement does not resolve materially different risk profiles. |

**Completion priorities:** Bluefen’s effective conditional consent, Riverlark repayment/security releases, verified share title and Ironquay IP ownership. Also reconcile the AUD 24m debt-free/cash-free price with debt, bonuses and other agreed adjustments before accepting the funds flow.
=== END ADVICE ===
